issues.description: Whole compiled script is shipped through the compile RPC response instead of a dedicated download endpoint.
issues.detail: The backend already writes the file to disk and returns its path; bolting script_content onto every compile response duplicates state, wastes memory and bandwidth, and threads file bodies through three layers of React state for a sometimes-used button. Add a download RPC keyed by path (or fetch on click) and let the browser do the work.

issues.description: open() lacks explicit encoding and error handling on a post-success read.
issues.detail: with open(script_path) as f: f.read() relies on the platform default encoding and has no guard, so a missing/unreadable/non-UTF8 file turns a successful compile into a failed RPC. Specify encoding='utf-8', state the UTF-8 invariant from compile_pipeline, and handle the read failure so it does not poison the compile result.

issues.description: Download icon is a clickable SVG, not a real button — no keyboard or a11y affordance.
issues.detail: GetAppIcon with onClick exposes no role, no keyboard handler, and no focus ring, unlike the adjacent 'Done' anchor. Wrap it in an IconButton/<button> with aria-label, or make it an <a download> matching the neighbor's shape so assistive tech and keyboard users can reach it.

issues.description: Filename derivation via split('/').pop() is fragile across platforms and trailing slashes.
issues.detail: compiledPath comes from os.path.relpath, which uses backslashes on Windows-hosted notebook servers, and a trailing slash yields an empty string. Either guarantee forward-slash at the server boundary or use a real basename helper rather than ad-hoc string splitting.

issues.description: Object URL and DOM anchor are not revoked on the exception path.
issues.detail: If a.click() throws under CSP or sandboxing, removeChild and revokeObjectURL never run, leaking a Blob URL and an orphan node. Wrap the create-anchor-and-click dance in try/finally so cleanup holds unconditionally, and add a brief comment documenting the idiom.

issues.description: Download icon renders unconditionally with no disabled/empty-content guard.
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick guards on compiledContent, but the icon always renders in the success branch. With an older backend or partial response, the click is a silent no-op. Gate rendering on compiledContent or show a disabled state so users get feedback instead of dead clicks.

synthesis.summary: Consensus verdict: NEEDS-WORK / WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE. The feature is small and useful but picks the wrong data flow — shipping the entire compiled script body through the compile RPC response and prop-drilling it through React state, when a path already exists and a dedicated download endpoint would compose cleanly with the browser's native download. The backend file read also lacks explicit UTF-8 encoding and error handling, so a post-success read failure poisons an otherwise successful compile. The frontend control is an SVG with onClick rather than a real button, breaking keyboard and assistive-tech access. Fix the data shape first; the rest follows.
